# Copilot Prompt Template: Generate a Project Page from a README

Use this template when you want GitHub Copilot to generate or refresh a project view page in this repo.

## Inputs

Choose **one** of the following modes.

### Mode A: Auto-fill from GitHub repo link (recommended)

- **GitHub repo link**: `<https://github.com/owner/repo>`
- **Today’s date (for sample headers/examples)**: `YYYY-MM-DD`
- **Content to omit** (optional): `[]` or e.g. `["license", "contributing", "fast dev loop"]`

If you only provide the GitHub repo link, Copilot must infer:

- **GitHub repo slug** from the URL (`owner/repo`)
- **Primary repo URL** from the URL
- **README raw URL** by trying common defaults in order:
  1) `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/refs/heads/main/README.md`
  2) `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/refs/heads/master/README.md`
  3) `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/refs/heads/main/readme.md`
  4) `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/refs/heads/master/readme.md`
  5) If the README lives elsewhere (e.g. `docs/README.md`) or the default branch is neither, ask me for the exact raw URL
- **Project display name** from the README title; fallback to repo name (kebab-case → Title Case)
- **Target file** name using the repo name in PascalCase:
  - Example: `adlist-parser` → `frontend/src/views/projects/AdlistParserView.vue`
  - Example: `plex-organizer` → `frontend/src/views/projects/PlexOrganizerView.vue`

### Mode B: Manual fill

- **Target file**: `frontend/src/views/projects/<ProjectName>View.vue`
- **Project display name**: `<Project Display Name>`
- **GitHub repo slug**: `<owner>/<repo>`
- **Primary repo URL**: `<https://github.com/owner/repo>`
- **README source**: 
  - Link: `<raw README URL>`
  - OR paste README content below.
- **Today’s date (for sample headers/examples)**: `YYYY-MM-DD`
- **Content to omit** (optional): `[]` or e.g. `["license", "contributing", "fast dev loop"]`

---

## Task

Generate (or update) the Vue 3 + TypeScript project page at **Target file** using the **README source** as the canonical content.

### Hard requirements (house style)

1. **Match existing project pages in this repo**
   - Use Vuetify layout with a single top-level `v-container`.
   - Use the shared components already used by other project pages:
     - `StatsAndChips` (GitHub stats)
     - `ButtonCard` (GitHub button)
     - `LinkableTitle` (section headings)
     - `LinkComponent` (inline links)
     - `InlineCode` (inline code)
     - `CodeBlock` (multi-line code blocks)
     - `TableOfContents` (local TOC component)
   - Optional (only when it matches existing pages and the README supports it):
     - `IconList` (feature lists)
     - `ImageCarosel` (screenshots)

2. **Local Table of Contents is required**
   - Always include `<TableOfContents />` at the end of the template **after** `</v-container>` and **before** `</template>`.

3. **Keep short code snippets inline**
   - If a snippet is short (one-liner, a couple of tokens), pass it directly into the component prop in the template.
   - Do **not** create script constants just to hold tiny strings.
   - Only create `const` values in `<script setup>` for:
     - Multi-line examples
     - Values used multiple times
     - Large tables/arrays (e.g. `v-data-table` items)

4. **README-driven content**
   - Use the README as the source of truth for features, usage, configuration, examples, and troubleshooting.
   - If the README includes sections that are in the “Content to omit” list, skip those sections.
   - Do not invent commands, flags, file paths, or performance numbers.

5. **Repo slug**
  - Set `const repo = '<owner>/<repo>'` in `<script setup>`.
  - Prefer lowercase for the slug (`toomas633/adlist-parser`), matching how other pages are written.

6. **Dates**
   - Any sample “Created/modified” header shown on the page should use **Today’s date**.

7. **Quality gates**
   - Output must be valid Vue SFC template (no broken tags).
   - Must pass TypeScript + ESLint in the `frontend/` project.

8. **Routing (only if requested or missing)**
  - If I ask you to “wire it up” (or if the route does not exist), also add the route entry following existing patterns in `frontend/src/router/projects.ts`.
  - If I did not ask to wire it up, only generate/update the view file.

---

## Page structure (follow this order)

Use this page layout unless the README strongly suggests otherwise:

1. Title + short description
2. Stats row + GitHub button
3. Table-of-contents anchors are generated by `LinkableTitle`; the TOC component is rendered at bottom
4. Sections (use `LinkableTitle`):
   - Features
   - Installation (optional)
   - Usage / Quick start
   - Configuration (if present)
   - Input/output formats (if present)
   - Performance / tuning (if present)
   - How it works / architecture (if present)
   - Troubleshooting / FAQ (if present)
   - Example output (if present)
   - Requirements (if present)
   - Use cases (optional, if present)
   - Acknowledgments (optional)

When something is not in the README, omit that section.

---

## Template scaffold (use as a guide, not literal text)

- Use this high-level structure:

```vue
<template>
  <v-container>
    <h1 class="text-center d-flex justify-center align-items-center">
      <Project Display Name>
    </h1>

    <StatsAndChips hide-langs :repo="repo" />

    <p :class="!isMobile ? 'text-center' : ''">
      <One-paragraph description from README>
    </p>

    <v-row class="d-block d-sm-flex" justify="center">
      <v-col class="align-content-space-around mt-3">
        <StatsAndChips hide-chips :repo="repo" />
      </v-col>
      <v-col class="align-content-space-around" lg="2" md="3" sm="4" xl="1">
        <ButtonCard
          text="GitHub"
          href="<Primary repo URL>"
          icon="mdi-github" />
      </v-col>
    </v-row>

    <LinkableTitle h1 title="Features" centered />
    <ul>
      <li>...</li>
    </ul>

    <LinkableTitle h1 title="Links" centered />
    <ul>
      <li>
        <LinkComponent href="<Primary repo URL>" text="GitHub repository" />
      </li>
      <!-- Add other links only if they exist in the README (e.g., docs, releases, Docker Hub). -->
    </ul>

    <!-- More sections... -->
  </v-container>

  <TableOfContents />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { isMobile } from '@basitcodeenv/vue3-device-detect'

const repo = '<owner>/<repo>'

// Large examples as const strings for <CodeBlock :code="..." />
// Tables as arrays for v-data-table, if needed
</script>
```

Notes:
- Do **not** add standalone `<v-divider ... />` between sections.
  - `LinkableTitle` renders the section divider by default.
  - Use `hide-divider` on `LinkableTitle` when you explicitly do not want a divider.
- Keep headings consistent: major sections use `h1`, subsections use `h2`.
- `ButtonCard` can be repeated for other key links (e.g. Docker Hub) if the README includes them.

---

## Content rules (important)

- Prefer bullets/lists for features and requirements.
- Prefer `CodeBlock` for multi-line code fences from README.
- If README has tables (formats/examples), consider a `v-data-table` only when it improves readability.
- Keep wording concise and accurate; remove marketing fluff.
- For inline links in paragraphs, prefer `LinkComponent` (matches existing pages).
- Only add image carousels / clickable images if you actually have local assets in `frontend/src/assets/images/...` (otherwise keep it simple and omit screenshots).

---

## Final checklist

- Includes `<TableOfContents />` after `</v-container>`.
- No broken template tags (`</li>`, `</ul>`, `</v-container>` etc.).
- Short snippets are inline; large ones are in script constants.
- Repo slug is correct and used for `StatsAndChips`.
- Any sample “Created/modified” date uses Today’s date.
- Sections in “Content to omit” are not included.

## Notes (repo-specific)

- Most shared components (e.g., `StatsAndChips`, `ButtonCard`, `LinkableTitle`, `CodeBlock`) are auto-registered in the frontend build; you typically **do not** need to import them in the view file.
- Do import only what you actually reference in `<script setup>`, commonly:
  - `isMobile` from `@basitcodeenv/vue3-device-detect`
  - types like `IconListItem` (and other local types) when building `IconList`/table data.
